annotations.title: What multiples did bankers use for comparable deals in this sector?

description: Use when the user is underwriting an entry or exit multiple, pricing an acquisition, or asks what similar companies sold for: "what EBITDA multiples are cybersecurity deals getting?", "what did bankers use as comps for CPG deals?". Reads the most recent merger proxies (DEFM14A) and S-4s that mention a precedent-transactions analysis and the sector, and returns every EV/EBITDA and EV/revenue range the advisors applied, the sentence it came from and a link to the filing. These are the advisors’ chosen comparables, not market prices, and are never averaged. Refuses before you are charged if no range can be read. Every result carries a run id, a date and a citation line. Calling this tool returns a quote, not the result: what the run measures, its price and a payment_url. The run happens only when you POST to payment_url, and a run that fails its controls refuses there with nothing charged. Dimensions (vary these inputs to cut the answer; each call is its own run): over time: built in: proxies over the last years; segment: sector or phrase. Price: $0.05 per run over x402 (USDC on Base, no account needed), or $0.50 over MPP (a Stripe shared payment token); charged only when the run comes back sound. For whether deal activity in the sector is rising, use run_deal_activity.
